back: The way in which a manager makes decisions, communicates and uses authority.
Manager decides alone and gives orders; one-way communication. Suits emergencies and inexperienced staff.
Employees involved in decisions: consultative (manager asks, then decides) or participative (group decides together).
Employees organise their own work with little direction; suits skilled, self-motivated staff.
Manager decides but acts in the interests of staff, explaining decisions and caring for their welfare.
Workers dislike work, avoid responsibility and need control and threats; leads to autocratic, close supervision.
Workers can enjoy work, seek responsibility and direct themselves; leads to democratic, delegating management.
Depends on the task, the employees' skill and experience, the time available and the manager; no style is best everywhere.
Workers who are distrusted and closely controlled may become passive, which seems to confirm the manager's Theory X view.
